item.title: Hikone Castle Cherry Blossoms: 1,000 Trees Around a National Treasure — Guide
item.description: Hikone Castle in cherry-blossom season is one of Shiga’s most beautiful sights: around 1,000 cherry trees bloom across the castle hill, ramparts and the surrounding moats each early April, framing the National Treasure keep in clouds of pale pink. The classic view is from the inner and outer moats, where boat rides and moat-side paths set the blossoms against the castle’s stone walls and the petals drift down to carpet the water, and the whole scene is lit after dark for yozakura evening viewing, making Hikone a fixture on lists of Japan’s finest hanami spots.

item.title: Nagahama Hikiyama Festival: Child Kabuki on Golden Floats — Guide
item.description: The Nagahama Hikiyama Festival, held each year in mid-April, is one of Japan’s three great float festivals and a UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage: its treasures are the hikiyama, towering gilded and lacquered ‘moving stages’ built in the 16th century, said to have begun when Toyotomi Hideyoshi celebrated the birth of an heir. What sets Nagahama apart is the performance — each float is a portable kabuki theatre on which local boys aged roughly five to twelve act out full classical kabuki dramas, mastering the stylised poses, voices and quick changes with a poise that draws gasps, cheered on by whole neighbourhoods.

item.title: Tohoku Cherry Blossoms Late April Early May 2026
item.description: Tohoku Cherry Blossoms Late April Early May: The Best Spots for Japan’s Most Spectacular Hanami Introduction: Why Tohoku Is Japan’s Best-Kept Cherry Blossom Secret If you’ve ever dreamed of standing beneath a canopy of cherry blossoms without fighting through crowds of thousands, Tohoku is where that dream comes true. While Tokyo and Kyoto grab international headlines every late March and early April, the Tohoku cherry blossoms in late April and early May offer something those famous cities simply cannot: space, authenticity, and a sense of wonder that feels undiscovered.
